title: Quantities and prices
goal: Buy food in specific quantities, ask how much things cost, and understand prices in dollars and euros.

items.fr: un kilo de, beaucoup de… + noun
items.en: quantity + de (no du, de la, des)

drills.en: I'd like a kilo of apples.
drills.explain: After a quantity, just [[de]]: [[un kilo de pommes]], not *des pommes*.

drills.en: He eats a lot of vegetables.

drills.text: Une bouteille ___ eau, s'il vous plaît.
drills.explain: Before a vowel, [[de]] becomes [[d']]: [[une bouteille d'eau]].

items.en: saying prices in dollars and euros

drills.explain: Say the dollars, then the cents: [[deux dollars cinquante]].
euros first, then the cents: [[trois euros vingt]].

blocks.title: At the Jean-Talon market in Montréal
blocks.context: Mei buys fruit and vegetables at a market stall.

lines.speaker: Marchand
lines.fr: Bonjour madame ! Qu'est-ce que je vous sers ?
lines.en: Hello, madam! What can I get you?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.en: Hello! How much are the apples?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Je voudrais un kilo de pommes, s'il vous plaît. Et cinq cents grammes de tomates.
lines.en: I'd like a kilo of apples, please. And 500 grams of tomatoes.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: C'est tout, merci. Ça fait combien ?
lines.en: That's all, thank you. How much is that?

lines.speaker: Marchand
lines.fr: Et voici trois dollars soixante-quinze. Merci, bonne journée !

blocks.title: After a quantity: just de
blocks.body:
When you give a **precise quantity** (a kilo, a bottle) or an **amount word** (a lot, a little, enough), French uses just [[de]] before the noun, with **no article**. [[de]] becomes [[d']] before a vowel.

- [[du lait]] → [[un litre de lait]]
- [[de l'eau]] → [[une bouteille d'eau]]
- [[des fruits]] → [[beaucoup de fruits]]

It's the same little [[de]] as after a negative: [[pas de viande]]. Think of [[de]] as “of”: a kilo **of** apples, a lot **of** fruit.

blocks.note: [[cinq cents]] = 500. You'll learn big numbers properly later; for now, learn [[cinq cents grammes]] as a chunk. You can also say [[un demi-kilo]].

blocks.title: Asking the price
blocks.pattern: Combien coûte + singular ? / Combien coûtent + plural ? / Ça fait combien ?
blocks.note: [[coûter]] (to cost) is a regular -er verb: [[il coûte]], [[ils coûtent]]; both sound the same. [[C'est combien ?]] works for everything. [[Ça fait combien ?]] asks for the **total** at the till, and the answer is [[Ça fait…]].

blocks.title: Saying prices
head: written
said
blocks.note: Say the big unit, then the cents, with no “and”: [[deux dollars cinquante]]. Don't say the comma. In Canada, [[cents]] (coins) is said like “sent”.

blocks.title: Prices in Canada
blocks.body:
- **Writing prices:** in French, the dollar sign goes **after** the number, with a space, and you use a **comma** for cents: [[2,50 $]]. In English, it's $2.50. You'll see both in Canada.
- **Taxes:** shelf prices don't include sales tax. At the till, the GST and (in Québec) the QST are added to taxable items: in French, [[la TPS]] and [[la TVQ]]. Basic groceries (fruit, vegetables, milk, bread) are usually not taxed, but snacks, soft drinks and restaurant meals are.
- **Cents:** [[un cent]], [[des cents]]. In Canada, this [[cent]] is said like “sent”, not like [[cent]] (100). In everyday Québec French, you'll also hear [[un sou]] or, informally, [[une cenne]].
- **Weights:** stores show prices per kilo **and** per pound ([[la livre]]): [[3,99 $ la livre]]. A pound is about 454 grams.

examples.fr: Les pommes, c'est deux dollars quatre-vingt-dix-neuf la livre.

blocks.body:
- [[un kilo des pommes]] is wrong: say [[un kilo de pommes]].
- [[beaucoup des fruits]] is wrong: say [[beaucoup de fruits]].
- [[deux dollars et cinquante]]: no [[et]] in prices. Say [[deux dollars cinquante]].
- [[une bouteille de eau]]: elide before a vowel → [[une bouteille d'eau]].
- Don't add -s to [[de]] in the plural: [[deux bouteilles de lait]]. Only the quantity word takes an -s.

blocks.title: Liaison with euros
blocks.body:
[[euro]] starts with a vowel, so numbers ending in a silent consonant **link** to it:

- [[un euro]]: “un‿n‿euro”
- [[deux euros]], [[trois euros]]: a **z** sound: “deu‿z‿euros”
- [[six euros]], [[dix euros]]: also a **z** sound
- [[vingt euros]]: a **t** sound: “vin‿t‿euros”

[[dollars]] starts with a consonant, so there's no liaison: [[deux dollars]] is “deu dollar”. The final s of [[dollars]] is silent.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Prices go fast in real life. Practise saying them smoothly, in one breath.

lines.tip: grammes: the final e and s are silent, say “gram”.
bouteille: the ill sounds like the y in “yes”.

No article after beaucoup de, and du is never used with a plural.

blocks.prompt: You're at a market stall. Ask the price of one item, buy three things with quantities, and ask for the total.
checklist: Three items with a quantity + de

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour ! Combien coûtent les tomates ? … Je voudrais un kilo de tomates, cinq cents grammes de fromage et une bouteille de jus d'orange, s'il vous plaît. C'est tout. Ça fait combien ? … Merci, bonne journée !
models.en: Hello! How much are the tomatoes? … I'd like a kilo of tomatoes, 500 grams of cheese and a bottle of orange juice, please. That's all. How much does it come to? … Thanks, have a good day!

blocks.prompt: Write a text message to your roommate: say what you need for dinner tonight (with quantities), and what you already have enough of.
checklist: On a besoin de… / J'ai besoin de…
At least three quantities (un kilo de, une bouteille de, un paquet de…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Sofia ! Pour ce soir, on a besoin d'un paquet de pâtes, de cinq cents grammes de poulet et d'une bouteille d'eau. On a assez de fromage et de légumes. Merci !
models.en: Hi Sofia! For tonight, we need a packet of pasta, 500 grams of chicken and a bottle of water. We have enough cheese and vegetables. Thanks!

summary:
- Use quantity + [[de]]: [[un kilo de pommes, une bouteille d'eau, beaucoup de fruits]]
- Ask [[Combien coûte… ?]], [[Ça fait combien ?]] and understand [[Ça fait…]]
- Say prices: [[2,50 $]] = [[deux dollars cinquante]], [[3,20 €]] = [[trois euros vingt]]
